# Source Descriptions — keep the text we already fetch

> ⚠️ **Status: In Review — awaiting Human Operator approval. No code may be written until Status = Approved** (Constitution Art. II).
> 
> Tier 0.1 and 0.2 of *Report — What the Metadata Source Offers That We Do Not Take*. The report ranked these first because they cost nothing: the values are already fetched and already discarded inside our own code.
> 
> ⚠️ Two items in one spec, deviating from the report's "each item its own spec". 0.2 is a single unread variable in the same file this spec already changes, and a spec of its own for it would be ceremony rather than rigour. Stated rather than done quietly.
## Intention
The plugin requests a scene's description, decodes it, maps it to `VideoMetadataProposal.notes` — and `VideoEnrichmentReview` never reads the field. Every match throws it away.
🔴 **The design question was settled by the Human Operator on 2026-08-08, and it is the whole of the difficulty.**
| Field | Whose | Rule |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `Asset.notes` (existing) | **The operator's own** | 🚨 Local to this app. **Never submitted anywhere, ever** — not now, and explicitly not in any future where a write path is reconsidered |
| a NEW field | The source's | Where a fetched description lands, clearly attributed |
⭐ The decision is not merely about avoiding an overwrite. **A private note is private in principle**, not by accident of nothing currently uploading it — so the boundary is drawn now, while the write path is out of scope, rather than argued about later when it might not be.
## 📊 Measured on the drive, 2026-08-09
|  |  |
| --- | --- |
| Videos | 2,077 |
| Carrying an identity | 1,378 |
| **With operator notes today** | **0** |
⚠️ **Zero is the number that matters, and it cuts against urgency rather than for it.** There is no conflict to resolve today, which is exactly why the separation is cheap to build now and impossible to retrofit later. The field must be right before the first note is written, not after.
## 🚨 D1 — Adopting this fills nothing retroactively
The most important thing about this change, and the report does not say it.
The descriptions were **discarded, not stored**. There is no cache to mine. So adopting 0.1 gives descriptions to videos matched *from now on*, and to already-matched videos only if they are refreshed — 1,378 of them.
⚠️ This must shape the expectation before the work is scheduled. Shipping it and finding 1,378 videos still blank would read as a broken feature rather than a correct one.
❓ **Open — is a backfill wanted?** *Refresh Matched Videos* already exists and fetches by known id, so this is 1,378 direct fetches and no human decisions. Recommend: ship the field first, measure how many new matches populate it, and decide the backfill against that. Sequencing a 1,378-request run behind an unproven field is the wrong order.
## D2 — The rule lives in the field's own documentation
⚠️ Not only in this spec, and not only in the report. A future reader weighing what to include in a submission payload will read `Asset.notes` and must find the answer **there** — the same discipline that keeps `credentialId` and the D9 rules stated at the point of use.
Both fields carry it: the operator's says it is never transmitted; the source's says it is not the operator's.
## D3 — Attribution travels with the text
Text from a source is attributed, the way `enrichmentSource` already attributes everything else. A description with no provenance becomes indistinguishable from something the operator wrote — which is the confusion this whole spec exists to prevent.
❓ **Open — one field or two?** A single `sourceDescription` plus the existing `enrichmentSource` is enough while there is one source per video. Recommend one field; revisit only if a video can be matched in two sources at once, which `video_match`'s (video, source) key already permits.
## D4 — It is a proposal, not an assignment
⚠️ It goes through the same review as every other proposed field: shown, tickable, refusable. A description that appeared without being accepted would be the first field in the app to write itself, and the review surface exists precisely so nothing does.
## Tier 0.2 — `releaseYear` is mapped and never read
A latent defect rather than a current loss. Our source supplies full dates, so `releaseDate` covers us — but a provider that knew only a year would have its date **silently ignored**, and the video would get no date rather than an approximate one.
⚠️ Dead code today, and worth fixing exactly because it is: the failure only appears when a second provider arrives, at which point it looks like that provider is broken.
🔴 **A year is not a date, and must not be stored as one.** Fabricating `YYYY-01-01` would make an approximation indistinguishable from a known day, and every consumer of `releaseDate` — the age-at-release filter, the original-versus-redistribution ordering — would silently treat it as exact.
❓ **Open:** store the year in its own field, or store nothing and surface the provider gap? Recommend the former only if a second provider is real; until then, make the discard EXPLICIT and reported rather than silent.
## Test strategy (Constitution Art. III)
- **S1** — 🚨 A fetched description never lands in `Asset.notes`. Asserted directly; it is the one irreversible interaction with operator-authored text.
- **S2** — An operator note survives a match, a re-match and a refresh untouched.
- **S3** — A description the operator does not accept is not written.
- **S4** — The stored description records which source it came from.
- **S5** — A source supplying no description leaves the field alone rather than blanking it.
- **S6** — A second match from the same source replaces the source's description and still does not touch the operator's note.
- **S7** — A year-only release value does not become `YYYY-01-01`, and is not silently dropped either.
## ✅ Decisions — 2026-08-09
The Human Operator accepted the recommendations as written. Recorded here as decisions rather than left as questions.
1. **D1 — no backfill up front.** Ship the field, let descriptions arrive with new matches, and decide a *Refresh Matched Videos* run against how many actually populate. ⚠️ Sequencing 1,378 requests behind an unproven field is the wrong order, and the run remains available at any time.
2. **D3 — ONE description field**, alongside the existing `enrichmentSource` for attribution. Revisit only if a video is ever matched in two sources at once, which `video_match`'s (video, source) key permits but nothing does today.
3. **0.2 — make the discard EXPLICIT, do not add a year field.** 🔴 A year is not a date and must never be stored as one: fabricating `YYYY-01-01` would make an approximation indistinguishable from a known day, and every consumer of `releaseDate` — the age-at-release filter, the original-versus-redistribution ordering — would silently treat it as exact. Until a second provider is real, the correct behaviour is to notice and report the gap rather than invent a value or drop it in silence.
